chapter: Police work, brass bands and carnival
title: Starting in brass bands and hiring the best men
summary: Williams says his first brass band job was around 1940 with Kid Howard and Lawrence Marrero, and that he paid better than scale to get the best players away from Sidney Diggs' band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well they don't sound right, those guys. They sound refined and classy and everything. Yeah. It makes a difference. When did you start playing in brass bands? We didn't get to that.

In brass bands? Oh, let's see. 1940. My first brass band job, when I played with Howard, I was playing with Howard. And then he and Lawrence, Lawrence Morell, and then they decided to form a brass band. Then I would play him with him. And in between time I'd play with Howard. You see? Then I was getting a lot of work myself, you see? And I never carried all the best Alvin Alcorn, Joe Phillip. I carried all the Hellfire fellas with me, you know? Because I had a lot of business in Sidney Diggs. You heard talk of Sidney Diggs. He had a Hellfire orchestra. Well I used to keep his band on the on crutches. I took one of his good men's buttons. I guess I probably just kept him on the Tato Point L. Oh yeah. I took him on the Tato Point L. Oh yeah. Mm-hm. another orchestra, William and Ricard. You see? Well me and Ricard used to get, Ricard Lexi, we used to pick out all the best men. You see, because we paid them more. The scale was six dollars and they were making ten with us, ten and twelve. We paid them nothing under twelve dollars, they made double. Well you know that made Sidney had to call somebody else to put in his place. We used to call him White Roach. White Roach. Yeah. Said well Roach won't see me tonight. Well Joe Phillip liked whiskey and Poe Pointer, he liked to drink and he'd be up all day and he might have parades, I'd use him on parades. They never turned on because you had the ideal boys, you had the square deal boys, I was one of the tops in the square deal because I played all that work. You had the jolly boys, you had the Liberty Bells. Well me, George, William and all of them, we were fighting in between them with them bids, you see, I mean, and all of them was carrying two bands. Well they got so they wouldn't let one man run two-liter speed, you know. So we had a doggone good then because if we catch an own union man working on a job, that was it. All we do is just jump right on in there and collect that fees and then they'd bring them before the board. They was much more stricken and the scale wasn't paying what it was paying.
